report.source_text: Laparoscopy demonstrated an SB mass adherent within the pelvis. Adhesiolysis was performed through a lower midline laparotomy to allow an oncological, stapled, side-to-side, antiperistaltic SB resection. The SB lumen was significantly narrowed by the mass, and multiple enlarged, firm mesenteric lymph nodes were palpable. There was no evidence of metastatic disease.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An octogenarian male with lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma presented to the emergency department with colicky abdominal pain, obstipation, nausea, and vomiting consistent with small bowel obstruction (SBO). He had a known history of an incidental non-obstructing small bowel mass identified 4 months prior. CT abdomen-pelvis with contrast confirmed a large obstructing distal small bowel mass that had increased in size compared to the prior study. He underwent diagnostic laparoscopy converted to lower midline laparotomy, revealing a mass adherent in the pelvis with significant luminal narrowing and enlarged firm mesenteric lymph nodes; no distant metastases were observed. An oncological stapled side-to-side antiperistaltic small bowel resection was performed. Postoperative histopathology confirmed a 75 mm grade 2 jejunal leiomyosarcoma with negative surgical margins. Of four lymph nodes examined, one demonstrated metastatic leiomyosarcoma while the remaining three showed features consistent with his known lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. EBV-encoded RNA was negative, excluding EBV-associated leiomyosarcoma. The patient progressed well and was discharged on postoperative day 7.
